## Research

### Selective Int8 Quantization for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
Independent research, VIT Chennai, on an NVIDIA H100 80GB (DST-FIST server).
Code: https://github.com/Sanjai-1903/moe-safe-band-quantization

A per-layer sensitivity probe scores each layer's quantization tolerance using
five signals (KL divergence, top-1 disagreement, choice-flip rate,
log-likelihood MAD, perplexity delta). Only the tolerant "safe band" is
quantized to int8 — 21 of 48 layers on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, 10 of 40 on
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B.

Multiple-choice benchmarks cannot separate selective from full int8: both score
91.5% on GSM8K and perplexity differs in the fourth decimal. Fidelity to the
unquantized bf16 model was measured instead, over 19,200 teacher-forced token
positions per config. Selective quantization wins all 12 fidelity metrics on
both architectures.

A fixed-layer-count control (every arm quantizes exactly 21 of 48 layers; only
the choice of layers varies, across the selected band, three random seeds and
the 21 most-sensitive layers) shows the selected band beating count-matched
random on 12 of 12 metrics. Paired over 150 prompts with 4,000 bootstrap
resamples: exact top-k expert set match improves by +6.52 points, 95% CI
[+6.31, +6.73], winning on 150 of 150 prompts.

Stated limitations: all-layer int8 still saves 15.6 GB more at equal perplexity
and equal accuracy, so the safe band's advantage is fidelity and throughput
rather than memory; on the Qwen models the sensitivity ranking correlates
strongly with depth (Spearman -0.852 and -0.947) and no last-N control arm has
been run; long-form output quality has not been measured.

### Where a MoE Model Can Afford to Lose Precision
Earlier phase, Apple silicon, four small MoE models, simulated int8.
Largest benchmark degradation anywhere in the phase: -0.66 percentage points,
with WikiText-2 perplexity unchanged at 6.67.

Layer-ablation finding: replacing layers with identity shows damage compounds
super-linearly. Four consecutive layers cost roughly seven times the sum of
their individual impacts, and three scattered layers (L3, L7, L11, +230.91%
perplexity) cost more than four adjacent ones (L4-7, +156.90%). Layer position
dominates layer count.

Caveats: the quantization was simulated (quantize then dequantize), so memory
savings are theoretical; the router was quantized too, which contaminates
routing conclusions drawn from this phase.

## Products and projects

- HireFaster — production AI resume-evaluation SaaS. Founder and lead
  developer. Next.js, FastAPI, MongoDB Atlas, Docker on AWS and Vercel, with
  SSE streaming, JWT auth, rate limiting, and fault-tolerant orchestration
  across three pipelines with automatic provider failover.
  https://hirefaster.giize.com
- GLI-Flow — open-source RTL-to-GDS ASIC design automation platform. React/Vite
  dashboard of 35+ views over a FastAPI REST backend, Docker, 82-file CI suite,
  and an LLM-assisted root-cause investigation engine for failed runs. Primary
  author, 15 of 17 commits, Apache-2.0.
  https://github.com/Sanjai-1903/gli-flow-1.0
- DriveCLIP — multi-task driving perception extending CLIP ViT-B/32 with a
  feature pyramid and cross-attention, merging five sequential tasks into one
  forward pass for 2.3x throughput at 20.4 FPS.
- RAG chatbot — retrieval-augmented assistant with vector search and embeddings.
  https://github.com/Sanjai-1903/rag-chatbot
- TinyLlama LoRA fine-tuning — parameter-efficient adaptation on Apple MLX with
  0.435% of parameters trainable.
  https://github.com/Sanjai-1903/fine-tuning-SLM
- Low-light animal detection — computer vision pipeline for wildlife detection
  under poor visibility.
  https://github.com/Sanjai-1903/animal-detection
